steam.hint: Paste your Steam profile URL, your SteamID64 or your custom name. The profile and the game details must be public, otherwise Steam won't let us read the library: in that case, sign in with Steam.

steps: Open the GOG login and sign in with your account.
You land on a blank page: copy the address from the browser bar.
Paste the address you copied here.
gog.wrong: That doesn't look like the right address: it should start with https and contain “code=”.
gog.note: You only do this once: from then on the connection renews itself.

steps: Open the Epic login and sign in with your account.
Some text appears on screen: select all of it and copy it.
Paste the text you copied here.
epic.wrong: That doesn't look like Epic's text: I need all of it, and it contains “authorizationCode”.
epic.note: You only do this once: from then on the connection renews itself.

steps: Open the Amazon login and sign in with your account. The store is the US one, but a non-US account signs in just fine.
You land on the amazon.com home page: copy the address from the browser bar.
Paste the address you copied here.
amazon.wrong: That doesn't look like the right address: it should contain “openid.oa2.authorization_code”.
amazon.note: Connecting registers an “AGSLauncher for Windows” device on your Amazon account, which you can remove any time from your Amazon settings. You only do this once.

steps: Sign in to playstation.com in your browser and tick “Trust this browser”.
Open the code page below: it shows a line like {"npsso":"…"}.
Copy the whole line, or just the value.
psn.wrong: I need the {"npsso":"…"} line or just the value. An empty npsso or an error means you are not signed in yet: sign in to playstation.com first.
psn.note: On PlayStation the connection expires if you don't import the library for about ten days. Automatic update keeps it alive; if you turn it off, you have to do this again.

steps: Open the Nintendo login and sign in with your account.
On the “Link an account” page do not click the red button: nothing happens. Right-click it and choose “Copy link address” (or “Copy link”, depending on the browser).
Paste what you copied here. It is good for about ten minutes.
nintendo.wrong: That doesn't look like the link address: did you click the button? I need the address that starts with “npf” and contains “session_token_code”.
nintendo.note: Ludex reads your digital library, including games you never launched, and the games you launched, cartridges included. A cartridge you never launched leaves no trace on Nintendo and has to be added by hand. You only do this once and the connection lasts about two years.

services.intro: Ludex makes nothing up: game data and libraries come from these services. We are not affiliated with any of them, and names and trademarks belong to their respective owners.
services.igdb: Game data provided by IGDB.com: titles, covers, genres, platforms, similar games.

software.title: Open source software
software.intro: Ludex is built on free software. These are the main parts, each with its own licence.
software.react: The interface, on the web and on the phone.
software.tanstack: The web app: routing, server rendering and data.
software.tamagui: The design system shared by web and mobile.
software.react-native-web: Runs the native components in the browser.
software.orpc: The typed link between client and server.
software.inter: The text typeface, served by Fontsource.
